implementation_notes: The dominant Rust answer is the typed-builder crate: deriving TypedBuilder generates a builder whose type parameters record which fields have been set, so omitting a mandatory field or setting one twice is a compile error while the field order stays free; #[builder(default)] marks optional fields. The generated builder is call-by-move and not Clone - it is a construction syntax, not a value to pass around. Choose it when presence and single-assignment are the requirement; a real sequence needs the typestate variant or the staged-type approach.
pitfalls: The derive reports a missing field as a deprecation notice rather than the headline error, so the real problem can hide below an unfamiliar first message; treat warnings as errors in CI.
The generated builder type carries many generic parameters and is deliberately not meant to be stored or passed around (call-by-move, not Clone).
Presence is checked, order is not: adding #[builder(default)] to a field that is logically required silently makes it optional.

variants.name: Hand-rolled typestate builder with PhantomData
variants.idiom_name: ConnBuilder<Stage, Data> + consuming transitions + PhantomData stage markers
variants.implementation_notes: Encode the current step in a type parameter with zero-sized markers: each transition consumes self (taking it by value) and returns ConnBuilder<NextStage, Data>, so calling a step out of order is a type error and the previous stage cannot be reused, while PhantomData carries the marker at no run-time cost. Use it when the order is a hard invariant or when adding the crate is undesirable; the trade-off is that the type signature grows with every step and the chain must be written as one expression, with explicit functions per branch point.
pitfalls: Consuming self means an intermediate builder cannot be stored and continued after a branch; control flow around one step needs a function returning the stage type.
Stage marker types must not be nameable by callers (keep them private or in a non-re-exported module): a caller who can spell ConnBuilder<Ready, _> can forge a finished state.
PhantomData is a compile-time marker only: the same data type is shared across stages, so the data must still be validated in build() (or in the transition) for value correctness.
